title: Class-wise Balancing Data Replay for Federated Class-Incremental Learning

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Two different formulas are both presented as 'the TTS loss' L_TTS. Eq. (7) applies a SEPARATE softmax to old-class logits and new-class logits (each normalized within its own block) and scales the whole sum by 1/(N_old+N_new). Eq. (9) applies a single softmax over the CONCATENATED old/new logits (Concat(f_old(x)/tau_old, f_new(x)/tau_new)) and scales the old block by 1/N_old and the new block by 1/N_new. These are mathematically distinct loss functions (separate vs joint normalization over classes), so a reader cannot tell which loss the method actually optimizes.

The prose states the server 'aggregates them into a global vector tau^i = concat{tau_k^{i,j}} and normalizes it to obtain a sampling distribution', but Eq. (6) normalizes p_k^{i,j} by a denominator that only sums over j' for a FIXED client k (sum_{j'=1}^{n_k^i}). A global normalization over the concatenated vector would require a denominator summing over all k and j. Per-client normalization gives every client equal total sampling mass regardless of client size, which is a materially different sampling scheme than the claimed global one and undermines the 'global-perspective' rationale of the GDR module.

Tables 2 and 4 report the same experimental settings (CIFAR100 5-task, TinyImageNet 10-task, same beta levels) but disagree in the beta=0.1 columns. For the full FedCBDR model on CIFAR100 beta=0.1, Table 2 reports 18.37 while Table 4 reports 46.40 (the latter equals Table 2's CIFAR10 beta=0.1 value, 46.40). Table 2 leaves TinyImageNet beta=0.1 blank for all methods while Table 4 fills it with 18.37 (Table 2's CIFAR100 beta=0.1 value). The Finetune row in Table 4 matches Table 2 position-by-position for all 8 values, confirming the data were copied positionally while the beta=0.1 column headers were relabeled. Either the Table 4 headers or the underlying data are wrong.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract / Section 5.4 vs Section 5.2 and Table 2
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract and Introduction claim 'yielding a 2%-15% Top-1 accuracy improvement' and Section 5.4 claims FedCBDR 'consistently outperforms other baseline methods across all task splits'. Section 5.2 itself acknowledges this is false: on CIFAR100 with 5 tasks and beta=1.0, FedCBDR (52.06%) underperforms LANDER (52.77%), a net -0.71% deficit. The absolute '2%-15% improvement' and 'consistently outperforms' claims are contradicted by the paper's own Table 2 and Section 5.2 text.

The Appendix Figure 7 (chart grid for CIFAR10/CIFAR100/TinyImageNet incremental-task accuracy) has a caption that reads 'Comparison of per-class sample distributions in the replay buffer between FedCBDR and Re-Fed on the CIFAR100 dataset... 10-task split and 5 clients', which describes per-class buffer distributions, not incremental-task accuracy. The caption is identical to Figure 8's caption (copy-paste error). The surrounding text (A.1.2) correctly describes Figure 7 as incremental-task performance, so the caption does not match the figure content.

The text states 'in task 1, while classes 10 and 18 contain nearly 100 samples each, class 11 has fewer than 10'. The accompanying per-class table for Task 1 shows Re-Fed values of class 10 ~100 (OK) but class 18 ~60 (not ~100), and class 11 ~30 (not 'fewer than 10'). The reported narrative numbers do not match the table it references.

The text claims a selected sample's weight is set to (1/sqrt(n_s * p_x)) e_x and that 'This adjustment ensures unbiased estimation during aggregation'. Standard inverse-probability (Horvitz-Thompson) weighting for unbiased re-weighted aggregation would use a scalar weight proportional to 1/p_x (or 1/(n_s p_x)); the printed 1/sqrt(n_s p_x) (with an e_x basis-vector factor) is not a standard unbiased weighting and is not shown to yield unbiased estimates. The 'unbiased estimation' claim is unsupported by the given formula.

Section A.1.6 states 'As shown in Table 9, LANDER suffers from significant forgetting...' but no Table 9 appears anywhere in the paper (Table numbering jumps from Table 8 to Table 11). Similarly, Appendix A.1.5 refers to 'Figure 9' but no Figure 9 image or caption is present in the document. The referenced artifacts are missing.

summary: The paper presents FedCBDR, a federated class-incremental learning method combining global-perspective data replay (GDR) with task-aware temperature scaling (TTS). Uncertainty-mode triage flagged equations, main result tables, and several appendix sections as high-risk; low-uncertainty snippets (intro/related-work prose, figure placeholders) were accepted without specialist findings. Verification found no result-invalidating algebraic error, but surfaced several internal inconsistencies that require author clarification: (1) Eq. 7 and Eq. 9 define two mathematically different TTS losses; (2) Eq. 6's claimed 'global' sampling normalization is actually per-client; (3) Table 4's beta=0.1 columns contradict Tables 2/3 for identical settings (FedCBDR CIFAR100 beta=0.1: 18.37 vs 46.40); (4) the abstract's '2%-15% improvement'/'consistently outperforms' claims are contradicted by the paper's own acknowledged underperformance on CIFAR100 5-task beta=1.0; (5) Appendix Figure 7's caption is mis-copied from Figure 8 and describes per-class distributions while the figure shows incremental-task curves; (6) A.1.3's narrative numbers (classes 10/18 ~100, class 11 <10) do not match its own table (~60, ~30); (7) the sampling-weight formula 1/sqrt(n_s p_x) is not standard unbiased importance weighting; and (8) Table 9 and Figure 9 are referenced but missing. Dataset statistics (Table 1), SVD dimensions (Eqs 1-5), the response to a citation sample, and most tables were verified consistent. Given lenient strictness and multiple medium-confidence findings (peak 0.75), the paper is flagged NEEDS_REVIEW rather than PASS; several items (Eq 7/9, Table 4, Figure 7 caption) are concrete enough that the authors should correct them before publication.
